recipes.reason: Wood is smoker fuel, not an edible ingredient.
ingredients: 4 whole chicken leg quarters, skin removed
steps: Combine seasonings. Set aside.
Brush chicken with mustard and press seasoning into both sides. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Preheat smoker to 225°F with forearm-sized mesquite wood chunks. Add chicken and insert a probe thermometer. Cook, adding wood as needed, until internal temperature reaches 170°F.
Move to a very hot grill and cook until charred and marked. Flip and repeat.
Serve immediately with desired side dishes.

recipes.reason: Wood is smoker fuel, not an edible ingredient.
ingredients: 1 ea. (4 pounds) boneless pork loin roast, trimmed of excess fat
steps: Combine salt, honey, and vinegar in a 6-quart container. Add ice, cover, and shake until ice is mostly melted and brine cools.
Add pork, toss to coat, and weigh down if needed. Refrigerate 3–3.5 hours.
Remove roast, rinse with cold water, and pat dry with paper towels.
Combine seasonings and sugar. Press into all sides of meat.
Preheat smoker to 200°F with forearm-sized hickory wood chunks. Add roast, cover, and cook until internal temperature reaches 135°F for medium rare.
Remove to a plate, cover tightly with foil, and rest 15 minutes before serving.
Remove okra tips and heads, and slice into ¼–½ inch wide pieces.
Sauté onion, celery, and bell pepper in butter until soft over medium heat, adding garlic shortly before onion softens.
Add okra and tomatoes. Stir to incorporate, adding a little water if dry.
Simmer over medium heat until okra is no longer sticky and stringy and becomes darker green.
Serve over rice or freeze for gumbo.

recipes.reason: Separate serving shells, dishes and tongs from edible ingredients, retaining optional mushroom caps.
ingredients: 24 small mushroom caps, trimmed and de-gilled (optional alternative to snail shells or dishes)
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Drain and rinse snails.
Blend butter with shallots, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper.
If using mushroom caps, sauté them in a little garlic butter until cooked but firm. Remove from heat.

Using 24 snail shells with serving dishes and tongs, put one snail in each shell and fill remaining space with garlic butter. Alternatively use 4 indented earthenware snail dishes, placing a snail and butter in each indentation. Or place 2–3 snails in each mushroom cap and top generously with garlic butter.
Heat in oven for 5–7 minutes and serve with French bread to soak up garlic butter.
